growth_story.headline: Egypt's income per person has grown a steady 2.2 percent a year since 1990, through a revolution, two currency upheavals and a Red Sea shock, to a new high.
growth_story.arc: Since 1990 Egypt's income per person has grown at about 2.2 percent a year with no lasting change in pace, more than doubling from 1,972 to 4,253 constant dollars, a level first reached in 2025 and its highest yet. Within that one long era there were sharp swings: growth ran at 4.8 to 5.2 percent a year in 2006–2008, then sat at or just below zero from 2011 to 2013, which the World Bank ties to policy uncertainty after the January 2011 revolution. Growth came back after the IMF-supported program of November 2016 let the pound float, and it averaged 2.6 percent in 2016–2025, against 2.3 percent in 2006–2015. From 2022 the IMF describes new strain from Russia's war in Ukraine and capital outflows, then Red Sea disruptions from December 2023 that cut Suez Canal earnings; inflation reached 33.9 percent in 2023 and growth in income per person fell to 0.6 percent in 2024. It picked up to 2.8 percent in 2025 after a move to a flexible exchange rate in March 2024, while investment fell to 11.7 percent of GDP in 2024 and 2025 and the IMF and World Bank keep pointing to the state's large role in the economy.

threads.title: Revolution and stalled years
threads.text: After the January 2011 revolution, income per person stopped growing: growth was -0.4 percent in 2011 and just below zero in 2012 and 2013. The World Bank links the slowdown to the fallout and policy uncertainty that followed, after faster growth in the late 2000s.

threads.title: The 2016 float and recovery
threads.text: In November 2016 Egypt began an IMF-supported program and moved away from a fixed pound, which the IMF said had been overvalued. Prices jumped, with inflation at 29.5 percent in 2017, but growth in income per person rose to 3.4 percent in 2018 and 3.7 percent in 2019.

threads.title: Outside shocks since 2022
threads.text: Russia's war in Ukraine set off capital outflows in 2022, and from December 2023 attacks on Red Sea shipping cut Suez Canal earnings. Inflation reached 33.9 percent in 2023 and growth in income per person slowed to 0.6 percent in 2024. In March 2024 Egypt moved to a flexible exchange rate.

threads.text: The IMF and the World Bank both describe a state that is heavily present in the economy, through many state-owned firms. Meanwhile investment fell from 18.8 percent of GDP in 2019 to 11.7 percent in 2024 and 2025.

since_last_year.text: The World Bank reports that growth picked up in the year to June 2026, led by household spending, investment, manufacturing and tourism. A regional conflict in early 2026 brought capital outflows and a weaker pound before conditions settled, and by October 2026 the World Bank said inflation was rising again.

growth_story.tension: The sources talk about growth in the whole economy, which the World Bank puts well above the growth in income per person in the data: 2.4 percent a year over 2006–2025. Most of the gap is the growing population, and the World Bank adds that new jobs have kept pace with only about half of the rise in working-age people. (World Bank, Macro Poverty Outlook, October 2026: "real GDP grew 4.4 percent annually, generating about 0.6 million jobs a year, roughly half the increase in the working-age population")
